A code host where every repository is an
Not a git wrapper. A different substrate.
Everything GitHub keeps in Postgres lives on the same streams as the code, under one unifying model — and the model is small enough to hold in your head.
A repo's main branch is an append-only stream. Branches are forks of the log at an offset — not copies of the tree. History is O(events).
Every change to a branch syncs to every user of that branch as it happens. An AI's edits appear while it types, not as a commit afterward.
Issues, wiki, pull requests, users, orgs — all events on streams. Every list view is a reducer over the log, rebuildable by replay. Lose every index, lose nothing.
The only way to change state is dispatching an event. Every session is a trace, every bug is an offset, time travel is a product feature.
Each project carries its task queue, its builder/critic loop, and the evidence of what has been proven — on the same streams as the code.
Nothing reaches verified on a builder's word. An adversarial critic interrogates the recorded run. Digests are compared with cmp, not eyeballs.
Built the long way. On purpose.
One model to hold them all.
. The whole stack, top to bottom:
Every noun — file, branch, repo, issue, wiki page, pull request, task, evidence — is the same thing: an entity defined by
repos · trees · files · PRs · issues · wiki · the loop, all live
authenticated, validated mutations · Auth0 answers only “who is this?”
issue boards, PR catalogs, registries — materialized by replay, never stored
metadata stream + per-file content streams · patches · forks · three-way merge
canonical JSON · opaque lexicographic offsets · SHA-256 state digests
the substrate — append-only, resumable, forkable; Electric Cloud in production
# terminal A dispatches; terminal B replays to the same digest
A real stream system — not an event log bolted on.
Plenty of things emit events. This one is made of them.
There is no `.git`. A branch is `(parent, forkOffset)`; merge is log-aware; “who changed what when” is a digest bisect, not archaeology.
// not a database with a changelog
Repo lists, issue boards, PR catalogs are derived streams. If a feature seems to need a database, the feature is misdesigned.
